name: audit-report
wording: a signed, content-free audit report (an in-toto Statement in a DSSE envelope) of a window of a chained fixture log, verified against the log as exported, after a later write, and under each tampering of the report or the log: the verdict each case gives, the check it fails at, how many tamperings were detected, and the sha256 of the envelope, fixed by the log, the clock and the key. A proof of concept on one fixture log with no model in the loop, never a hypothesis result
filed_under: research/results/h1-* only because research/tests/test_prereg.py maps every MANIFEST file to one hypothesis's results glob; the result decides no hypothesis, as card E8.16 filed its leak count
tampering: a count in the statement changed, not re-signed
the statement re-signed under another key
a false count signed with the operator's key
a head beyond the chain, signed with the operator's key
an event edited in the log
an event edited and the chain rehashed
an event edited, the chain rehashed and the checkpoints deleted
limits: One fixture log of seven events under the test policy, on SQLite, with a seeded salt source and a fixed Ed25519 key; the core suite also runs the acceptance cases on Postgres, which this record does not cover.

The tamperings are those a person with database access and the code but not the operator's private key can make, plus a report re-signed by the key holder with a false count; an operator who holds the key and rewrites the whole log before exporting is detected only by a checkpoint held outside the database (ADR 0038).

The report is exported with the fixture's reader declared to the oracle (person:dana, member of person:dana and team:platform), so its oracle count is judged with her memberships; with no actor declared a report states no oracle count. The log is chain version 2 (card E1.9).
